Plugin Reference > deno — Deno-Compatible API Plugin

deno — Deno-Compatible API Plugin

Zig 0.17This plugin is built with Zig 0.17: the 0.17 branch builds successfully with Zig 0.17 and passes the Zig unit tests; the old 0.14.1 branch is left untouched.

sa_plugin_deno is a native SA replacement surface for Deno-style system capabilities. In the words of its API_COVERAGE.md: "a native SA replacement surface for Deno-compatible APIs. It does not call the deno executable or embed the Deno runtime" — it does not invoke the deno executable and does not embed the Deno runtime; instead it implements, natively in Zig, a subset that SA programs can call directly through the C-ABI. This page gives the real composition of its 57 externs, a grouped panorama of its 175 DENO_* macros, its four-tier coverage ledger, and how it differs from Deno's native permission system.

NoteThis plugin has no README. The authoritative sources are sap.json (capability sections and permissions), deno.sai/deno.sal (contract and macro facade), API_COVERAGE.md (coverage ledger), and the four-plugin joint evaluation document docs/plugin_evaluation_cn.md (2026-06-15). All figures on this page are labeled with their source and date basis.

1. The Real Composition of the 57 Externs

deno.sai has 68 lines in total and 57 @extern declarations (measured for this page), but they are not all the same kind of thing. Following the section comments inside the file, they split into three blocks:

Group (by the comments inside deno.sai)CountContent
Core Deno surface (from the start of the file to command_exec)36 Buffer release free_buffer; system information hostname / os_release / os_uptime / loadavg / system_memory_info / network_interfaces / pid / ppid / uid / gid / exec_path / memory_usage; environment variables env_get / env_set / env_delete; files read_text_file / read_file_base64 / write_text_file / write_file_base64 / mkdir / remove / copy_file / read_dir_json / lstat_json; miscellaneous random_uuid / args_json / btoa / atob / text_encode / text_decode / version_json / build_json / now_ms / now_ns; processes command_exec
"New migrated Deno FFI APIs" (the migration supplement section)8 cwd / chdir / version_deno / build_os / build_platform_family / date_now_iso / make_temp_dir / make_temp_file
chat / responses / MCP helpers13 chat_sse_to_responses / chat_json_to_responses / responses_sse_normalize(_with_request) / responses_json_normalize(_with_request) / responses_request_normalize / responses_chat_fallback_request / mcp_server_status_list / mcp_tool_call / mcp_resource_read / infer_collaboration_mode / jsonrpc_params_string_literal. This group has nothing to do with the Deno namespace; it is a set of LLM gateway / MCP message normalization helpers (see the mission-drift note below)

Scale comparison (the table in the evaluation document “Four-Plugin Evaluation”, 2026-06-15, + measurements for this page, 2026-08):

MetricValueBasis
Zig source5,155 lines (measured); of which src/hubproxy_compat.zig is 3,961 lines and src/deno_saasm_api.zig is 1,077 lines The evaluation document records 5,123 lines, with hubproxy at 77%
Macro facadedeno.sal is 984 lines with 175 [MACRO] entries (measured) The evaluation document records a 959-line facade
Artifactszig-out/lib/libdeno.so / zig-out/bin/deno.dll artifacts in sap.json
SA-side testsNone. tests/ contains only deno_windows_test.zig (Zig unit tests for the Windows target) The evaluation document records “no standalone tests/”
WarningMission drift: Section 3.3 of the evaluation document points out that about three quarters of the deno plugin's Zig code, in hubproxy_compat.zig, does MCP (JSON-RPC) / LLM gateway message compatibility rather than the Deno API surface; the third group of 13 externs above is its exposure at the contract layer. When using it, treat that part as an independent capability domain, not as part of “Deno compatibility”.

2. Three-Layer Call Architecture: Who Is Working Behind One Macro

The header imports of deno.sal explain its real structure: @import "deno.sai", "sa_http_client.sai", "sa_http_server.sai", "sa_std/io.sai", "sa_std/net.sa", "sa_std/process.sai", and "sa_std/time.sai". The DENO_* macros therefore take three implementation paths:

LayerSymbols reachedMacro families
① The plugin's own C-ABIsa_deno_plugin_* (exported by libdeno.so) System information, env, text/binary files, directory metadata, encoding, JSON snapshot family, temp, cwd/chdir, DENO_COMMAND_EXEC, the chat/MCP group
② Reused sibling pluginssa_http_client_* (HTTP/1.1+TLS, Zig std backend), sa_http_server_* (localhost HTTP/1.1 server) The full DENO_HTTP_* set, the full DENO_SERVE_* set, and the DENO_FETCH_* / DENO_REQUEST_* / DENO_HEADERS_* / DENO_RESPONSE_* alias layer
③ Reused SA standard librarysa_net_tcp_listener_bind / _accept / tcp_connect / …_close, sa_std_process_run/spawn/wait/read_stdout/close, sa_io_stdout/stderr/stdin/write_all, sa_time_sleep_ms, sa_json_parse / sa_json_stringify, and sci's NET_WS_* / NET_URL_PARSE macros DENO_LISTEN_TCP / ACCEPT_TCP / CONNECT_TCP / CLOSE_TCP_*, DENO_COMMAND_RUN/_SPAWN/_WAIT/_READ_STDOUT/_CLOSE, DENO_STDOUT/STDERR/STDIN(_WRITE), DENO_SLEEP_MS, DENO_JSON_PARSE/STRINGIFY, DENO_WS_FRAME_*, DENO_URL_PARSE
NoteTwo semantic details that are easy to trip over: (1) DENO_EXIT %code expands to panic(%code) — an abnormal termination, not a clean exit-code channel; (2) TCP listening/connecting and child-process spawn use sa_std/sci runtime primitives, and are not bound by the sa_deno_plugin_* status-code convention (the return structure is an i32 status + u64 handle packed into a 16-byte result block, split apart inside the macro with two loads).

deno.sai also defines four method constants (verbatim): #def DENO_HTTP_METHOD_GET = 1, POST = 2, PUT = 3, and DELETE = 4, for use as the method argument of DENO_HTTP_REQUEST_NEW / DENO_FETCH_REQUEST_NEW.

This page classifies each of the 175 [MACRO] entries in deno.sal individually; the counts in the table below sum to exactly 175. Parentheses after a macro name give that family's aliases/SYNC variants; the representative parameter column reproduces the first line of the [MACRO] header, so the call order can be checked directly:

Environment variables (3) DENO_ENV_GET / ENV_SET / ENV_DELETE DENO_ENV_GET %out_ptr, %out_len, %out_status, %key, %key_len
Text / binary file reads and writes (10) DENO_READ_TEXT_FILE(_SYNC), DENO_READ_FILE(_SYNC), DENO_WRITE_TEXT_FILE(_SYNC), DENO_WRITE_FILE(_SYNC), DENO_READ_FILE_BASE64, DENO_WRITE_FILE_BASE64 DENO_READ_TEXT_FILE %out_ptr, %out_len, %out_status, %path, %path_len; DENO_WRITE_TEXT_FILE %out_status, %path, %path_len, %data, %data_len
Directories and metadata (18) DENO_MKDIR(_SYNC), DENO_REMOVE(_SYNC), DENO_COPY_FILE(_SYNC), DENO_READ_DIR_JSON / READ_DIR_SYNC_JSON / READ_DIR / READ_DIR_SYNC, DENO_LSTAT_JSON / LSTAT_SYNC_JSON / LSTAT / LSTAT_SYNC, DENO_STAT_JSON / STAT_SYNC_JSON / STAT / STAT_SYNC DENO_MKDIR %out_status, %path, %path_len, %recursive; DENO_LSTAT_JSON %out_ptr, %out_len, %out_status, %path, %path_len. 4. The Four-Tier Coverage Ledger

API_COVERAGE.md divides the whole Deno surface into four tiers (the following is a translation of that document's key points, verbatim in substance):

TierMeaningContent listed in that document
implementedA native implementation exists and can be used directly host/sys information, pid/ppid/uid/gid, memory usage, env get/set/delete, text file read/write, random UUID, args JSON, base64 helpers, text encode/decode byte helpers, version/build JSON, wall clock, mkdir/remove/copy/readDir/lstat, command output
planned_nativeA native replacement is planned but currently missing The remaining stable namespace APIs, in particular cwd/chdir, chmod/chown, rename, binary read/write, stat/realPath/readLink/symlink/truncate, temp files/dirs, umask/kill, DNS, permissions, file handles, network handles
stub_unsupportedExplicitly not done (compatibility would require a larger subsystem) test/bench registration, the full Web APIs, WebGPU, KV, lint, Jupyter, browser-style event objects
type_onlyTypeScript type helpers only, with no runtime symbol to map TS helper types that map to no SA symbol
WarningThis ledger lags behind the contract files: the cwd/chdir/temp files/dirs named under planned_native already appear in the migration section of deno.sai and in the deno.sal macros (this page has verified that the symbols exist); while the DENO_STAT* macros are in fact only aliases of lstat, and binary read/write exists only as the base64 variant. When checking capabilities, take deno.sai/deno.sal as authoritative and treat API_COVERAGE.md as a lead.

5. The Permission Model: Similarities and Differences with Deno's Native Permission System

The ledger declared in sap.json (enforced by the host at load/call time):

DimensionDeclared content
fsThe four operations read / write / create / delete on $PROJECT/** (note: unlike node — Node.js Compatibility Facade, there is no metadata operation here, so the paths that lstat-style calls depend on must fall inside the project directory)
nethttps://*, http://localhost, and http://127.0.0.1, with a method allowlist of the seven methods GET / POST / PUT / PATCH / DELETE / HEAD / OPTIONS
envOnly HOME, PATH, SA_*
process"spawn": true, with an exec allowlist of only /usr/bin/env (arguments unrestricted, *)
Capability sectionsdeno.sys, deno.env, deno.fs, deno.process

Comparison with Deno's native permission system:

DimensionNative Denosa_plugin_deno
Authorization timingRuntime CLI flags (--allow-read etc.) + an interactive prompt A static declaration at install time, hardcoded in sap.json and enforced by the host; a program cannot add authorization from inside
Runtime query / requestDeno.permissions.query()/request(), with the three states granted/denied/prompt No corresponding extern. API_COVERAGE.md lists permissions explicitly in the planned_native tier
Filesystem granularity--allow-read=/any/path can point at any directory Only $PROJECT/**; no metadata operation
Network granularity--allow-net=host:port, precise to host and port https://* opened as a whole + plaintext HTTP limited to two local addresses; no port-level constraint exists in the declaration
Child-process granularity--allow-run=program authorizes by program list /usr/bin/env with arbitrary arguments — the evaluation document points out that this amounts to an escape hatch, because env itself can launch arbitrary commands
System information--allow-sys gates Deno.hostname()/uid() etc. Carried by the deno.sys capability section, with no second check at the symbol level

What they share: both follow the idea of deny by default, explicit authorization, and both treat fs/net/env/run/sys as independent dimensions. The essential difference is this: Deno makes permissions a capability negotiable at runtime, while the SA plugin model moves them forward into a static install-time ledger — so porting code that relies on dynamic Deno.permissions probing requires changing it to the assumption of “check sap.json first, then call”.

6. Installation and Verification

# 在 D:/projects/sla/sa_plugin_deno 内执行
SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa plugin install --dev .
sa plugin list          # 确认 deno 已安装
sa skills --json        # 确认 deno.sys / deno.env / deno.fs / deno.process 四段已加载
zig build               # 构建 libdeno.so / deno.dll

The test step is registered only for the Windows target. In build.zig, b.addTest/b.step("test", …) are wrapped inside the if (target.result.os.tag == .windows) branch and run tests/deno_windows_test.zig: that is, on Linux zig build test has no runnable test step. What that test covers (assertion points, reproduced): the plugin descriptor is named deno and the ABI version matches; os_release returns "Windows" and build_platform_family returns "windows"; pid > 0, and hostname/cwd are non-empty; env_get("TEMP") successfully returns a buffer that must be released with free_buffer, and a missing key gives status code 1; on Windows, uid/gid always return 0. This also yields two useful contract facts in passing: string output parameters are allocated by the plugin and must be released with sa_deno_plugin_free_buffer; status code 1 means the query target does not exist (e.g. a missing environment variable).

NoteThe end of API_COVERAGE.md requires running "run tests/deno-symbol-interface-smoke.sh" when adding an extern, but that script does not exist in the repository (verified for this page with a whole-repository find). For a contract audit you can only compare by hand: the symbols declared in deno.sai vs the exports from nm -D --defined-only zig-out/lib/libdeno.so.

7. Call Forms (No Ready-Made SA Examples; the Following Is Derived from the Contract)

WarningThe repository contains no .sa examples or tests at all: tests/ holds only the Windows Zig unit tests, and docs/ has no demos either. This section is therefore not a “copy-and-run example”, but a call form derived from the real macro definitions in deno.sal; the macro bodies themselves are verbatim excerpts of real code, and the skeleton parts are marked as illustrative.

The real expansion shape of a macro (verbatim from D:/projects/sla/sa_plugin_deno/deno.sal, showing the fixed pattern of “stack_alloc output slots → call → load back”):

[MACRO] DENO_READ_TEXT_FILE %out_ptr, %out_len, %out_status, %path, %path_len
    __rf_ptr_slot = stack_alloc 8
    __rf_len_slot = stack_alloc 8
    %out_status = call @sa_deno_plugin_read_text_file(&%path, %path_len, &__rf_ptr_slot, &__rf_len_slot)
    %out_ptr = load __rf_ptr_slot+0 as ptr
    %out_len = load __rf_len_slot+0 as u64
[END_MACRO]

[MACRO] DENO_CONNECT_TCP %out_status, %out_stream, %host, %host_len, %port
    __deno_connect_res = call @sa_net_tcp_connect(&%host, %host_len, %port)
    %out_status = load __deno_connect_res+0 as i32
    %out_stream = load __deno_connect_res+8 as u64
[END_MACRO]

Illustrative call form (assembled following the parameter order in the table above; the path must fall inside $PROJECT/**):

@import "deno.sal"

L_ENTRY:
    // 读文本文件：出参在前（ptr/len/status），入参在后（path/len）
    data_ptr = add 0, 0
    data_len = add 0, 0
    st1 = add 0, 0
    EXPAND DENO_READ_TEXT_FILE_SYNC data_ptr, data_len, st1, path_buf, path_len_val

    ok1 = eq st1, 0            // 状态码 0 = 成功；字符串缓冲由插件分配
    br ok1 -> L_USE, L_ERR     // 用完须 EXPAND DENO_FREE_BUFFER data_ptr, data_len, stf

L_USE:
    // 环境变量：键缺失时状态码为 1（见 deno_windows_test.zig 的断言）
    val_ptr = add 0, 0
    val_len = add 0, 0
    st2 = add 0, 0
    EXPAND DENO_ENV_GET val_ptr, val_len, st2, key_buf, key_len_val
    // …… TCP 连接则走 sa_std 返回块：
    // EXPAND DENO_CONNECT_TCP st3, stream, host_buf, host_len_val, port_val
    return
L_ERR:
    panic(st1)

The only executable verification is tests/deno_windows_test.zig, which demonstrates the correct grip at the C layer (allocate a ?[*]const u8, check for a returned u32 0, slice by length, then call free_buffer), for example:

fn readOwned(comptime function: anytype) ![]const u8 {
    var ptr: ?[*]const u8 = null;
    var len: u64 = 0;
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(u32, 0), function(&ptr, &len));
    const bytes = (ptr orelse return error.NullBuffer)[0..@intCast(len)];
    const copy = try std.testing.allocator.dupe(u8, bytes);
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(u32, 0), plugin.sa_deno_plugin_free_buffer(ptr, len));
    return copy;
}

8. Explicit Out-of-Scope Items

  • The whole stub_unsupported group: test/bench registration, the full Web APIs, WebGPU, KV, lint, Jupyter, browser-style event objects — these would require a larger native subsystem to be compatible with, and the plugin explicitly does not do them.
  • The parts of planned_native that have not yet landed: chmod/chown, rename, real binary read/write (currently only the base64 variant), stat/realPath/readLink/symlink/truncate, umask/kill, DNS, permissions, file handles, network handles. Of these, stat is currently only an lstat alias, and DNS and network handles are entirely absent — when porting code that uses the Deno.stat() and Deno.connect() abstractions, you must fill these in yourself.
  • No Deno-style object model: the WebSocket class, TLS/production listening for Deno.serve(), and the Request/Response object semantics of fetch do not exist. The macro layer has only frame-level helpers and one-shot JSON/slice responses; serve uses the localhost-only http-server — Embedded HTTP Server.
  • The MCP/chat helpers are not part of the Deno compatibility surface: 13 externs / 12 macros come from hubproxy_compat.zig (about 3,961 lines, the bulk of the plugin's Zig source). The evaluation document recommends splitting them out into an independent plugin, so the “Deno compatibility” narrative is not diluted.
  • Dynamic permission negotiation: Deno.permissions.query()/request() has no counterpart; privileges cannot be escalated at runtime.
WarningThe evaluation document's (2026-06-15) conclusion on the four plugins applies here too: the deno plugin should be positioned and presented as an experimental subset — “a Deno subset, not the Deno runtime”. Its ABI design (handle + poll/take/free, explicit free_buffer) is clean, but it lacks an end-to-end compatibility smoke test, and its core IO has obvious gaps. Before choosing it, first self-test with the install and build commands in Section 6, then check the Section 4 ledger to confirm which tier the APIs you need are in. When you need HTTP client capability, you can also consider the smaller and more trustworthy http-client — HTTP Client directly.
